comments.rawMarkdown: Yes, publishing derived labels is okay.

replies.rawMarkdown: Follow-up: may a paper-track resource publish machine translations (6 languages) of the public training tasks’ problem statements, keyed by instance_id, with code/identifiers/tracebacks kept verbatim? No patches, test patches, or hints. If not, is releasing only the translation script + per-item QA flags (participants regenerate the text from the competition data) acceptable?
replies.content: Follow-up: may a paper-track resource publish machine translations (6 languages) of the public training tasks’ problem statements, keyed by instance_id, with code/identifiers/tracebacks kept verbatim? No patches, test patches, or hints. If not, is releasing only the translation script + per-item QA flags (participants regenerate the text from the competition data) acceptable?

replies.rawMarkdown: I believe the preferred method would be publish the translations keyed by instance_id and link to the original dataset for the verbatim components (or via a script that downloads it).
replies.content: I believe the preferred method would be publish the translations keyed by instance_id and link to the original dataset for the verbatim components (or via a script that downloads it).

replies.rawMarkdown: Thanks! We’ll release prose translations with placeholders for all verbatim spans, plus a script that restores them from the competition’s tasks.jsonl.
replies.content: Thanks! We’ll release prose translations with placeholders for all verbatim spans, plus a script that restores them from the competition’s tasks.jsonl.

firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
Hi organizers. I'm preparing a paper-track submission on issue-to-function localization. For the local training tasks, I derived labels listing which functions/classes each upstream fix edits (instance ID → file/symbol paths). The labels contain no problem statements, patches or test content.

Rule 2.4(b) says Competition Data shouldn't be redistributed to non-participants. Is it OK to publish these derived labels, or should I release only code that rebuilds them from the public upstream PRs?
